subject: Parental consent & youth data processing statement
messages:
From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@playlearn.app>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: youth data processing & prohibited-use confirmation

Hi Jonas,

Hope youre well. Were finalizing our procurement and need a short written confirmation from Redwood about how you handle accounts and data from users under 16 (we have EU children user flows as well). Specifically: 

- Confirmation that Redwood does not knowingly target children under 13 and does not permit under-13 accounts without parental consent.
- A short description of age-gating / parental-consent workflows you support (server-side checks, token gating, delegated parent consent flows, PII handling).
- Any SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ references or attachments relevant to our privacy team.

We need the attestation and any evidence (flow diagram or short policy excerpt) by next Friday to keep our onboarding timeline. If an attestation PDF is available, thatd be ideal.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Johnson
Senior PM, Trust & Safety
PlayLearn, Inc.

Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: youth data processing & prohibited-use confirmation

Jonas / Laura / Dev — I drafted responses and populated PlayLearns attestation. Key points included (see attached excerpts to paste into their PDF):

- Redwood does not knowingly facilitate under-13 accounts by default; our Console exposes an account-age flag and a server-side gating hook that customers can enable.
- We support parental-consent workflows via a server-side consent callback and a delegated consent token (designed to integrate with customer-built parent verification). We do not provide first-party parental verification services.
- For EU/different thresholds (e.g., 16), customers may configure a higher age threshold; the same gating hooks apply.
- Data retention and processing for underage accounts follow the customers DPA: we segregate customer data and honor deletion/portability requests triggered by the controller.
- Referenced artifacts: SOC 2 report (available under NDA), SIG Lite answers (link), and CAIQ snapshot (published in our security portal). We included a short excerpt from the DPA and SCC clauses about controller/processor roles.

Attachments to include when returning to PlayLearn: playlearn_consent_flow.png, DPA_SCC_excerpt.pdf, and a signed PlayLearn_Youth_Data_Attestation.pdf.

Laura — can you export the gating flow PNG and add the callout text for the consent token?
Jonas — once final, Ill sign/approve the attestation.

Thanks,
Priyom
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: policy@playlearn.app, Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@playlearn.app>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Completed: Youth-data attestation + supporting artifacts (PlayLearn)

Emma / PlayLearn Policy Team — thanks for the template. Attached is the completed PlayLearn_Youth_Data_Attestation.pdf signed by Redwood Legal, plus two supporting artifacts: a one-page consent flow (playlearn_consent_flow.png) and an excerpt from our DPA/SCCs that references controller/processor responsibilities (DPA_SCC_excerpt.pdf).

Summary (for quick review):
- Prohibited use: Redwood does not accept or provision accounts that it knows to belong to children under 13 without parental consent. We offer server-side gating hooks and token-based delegated parental-consent flows that customers can enable in Console.
- EU differences: customers can set the age threshold to 16 in their tenant settings; the gating and consent callbacks are identical.
- Evidence: SOC 2 report and SIG/CAIQ artifacts are available upon NDA; we included the DPA excerpt that specifies data deletion/retention obligations for controllers.

Next steps: if youd like a short technical session to walk through the webhook and token examples, Laura and Dev can host a 30-min call next week.

Attachments: PlayLearn_Youth_Data_Attestation.pdf, playlearn_consent_flow.png, DPA_SCC_excerpt.pdf

Best,
Jonas Weber
